proposed_from.topic: Leaky-IV tangent-contact inference in Watson et al.'s p=2 linear SEM. Let delta=tau^2-tau_check^2 approach zero over explicit local triangular arrays. Define the total positive-part plug-in interval on empirically infeasible samples, derive its exact square-root Gaussian endpoint law, derive the distinct data-dependent retained-resample kernel used by leakyIV, and prove ordinary/discarded bootstrap nonuniformity. Construct a multiplier score-inversion confidence hull with uniform whole-identified-set coverage, matched n^-1/4 minimax outer directed-Hausdorff loss at contact, root-n loss in the fixed interior, and adaptation by the same one-dimensional procedure. Use the explicit positive-definite Sigma(a) witness and exclude weak instruments by a fixed relevance bound. PRESOLVE EVIDENCE REQUIRING VERIFICATION: In the Gaussian witness, X=Z1+epsilon_x and Y=aZ2+epsilon_y imply sqrt(n)(delta_hat-delta_n) converges to N(0,4) along a_n^2=1-h/sqrt(n); after n^1/4 scaling the ordered endpoints become plus/minus sqrt((h+Z)_+). Conditional on the first-stage realization, retained bootstrap endpoints instead follow a random truncated kernel, establishing a concrete nonuniformity mechanism. A uniform score error r expands quadratic-contact sets by order sqrt(r) and interior sets by order r, so one root-n score hull plausibly adapts between n^-1/4 and n^-1/2. LAN contiguity along the witness supplies the converse route. UNRESOLVED BOTTLENECK: Prove one uniform multiplier approximation for the quadratic score process over both contact-local and interior classes that yields simultaneous whole-set coverage and expected outer-loss bounds under the same critical-value rule. EARLY KILL TEST: On the one-parameter Gaussian witness, prove uniformly for h in a fixed compact set that the score hull covers the entire interval with worst expected outer loss of order n^-1/4 and that the retained bootstrap has the stated random truncated kernel; pivot or stop if either assertion fails.
proposed_from.novelty_justification: The exact \(p=2\) score reduction and the \(K\)-intersected raw endpoint representation on its proper nonnegative-slack domain are credited entirely to Watson et al.'s Corollary 2.1 and Appendix A.7. The novelty kernel starts with the fourth-root positive-part Gaussian endpoint law and the random truncated kernel generated by the fully specified finite Monte Carlo version of the feasibility-retained workflow in their Theorem 4, followed by a direct contact-nonuniformity result for that workflow. The constructive advance is one totalized quadratic-score hull with conditional uniform whole-set coverage and automatically changing expected outer-loss rates, matched by fully quantified contact and interior Gaussian LAN lower bounds. Li's proximal bootstrap does not subsume this kernel because it treats root-\(n\) constrained point estimators rather than partially identified sets.

seed_details.title: One-rule multiplier score hull with contact-to-interior adaptation
seed_details.anchor: watson2024bounding, Corollary 2.1, Theorem 4, and Appendix A.9
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Invert the regular quadratic leakage score before applying the square-root endpoint map, then prove one conditional multiplier coupling over contact-local and fixed-interior laws.
seed_details.search_result: Romano--Shaikh and Chernozhukov--Newey--Santos establish general set or constrained-model inversion; Li treats constrained point estimators. None gives this leaky-IV whole-set hull or its adaptive directed-Hausdorff rates.
seed_details.red_team: Immediate from generic criterion inversion because the score is finite dimensional.
seed_details.rebuttal: Generic coverage does not supply the half-Hölder score-to-set modulus, the common expected-loss bound, or the matched contact/interior frontier.

seed_details.title: Exact contact endpoint law and retained-resample kernel
seed_details.anchor: watson2024bounding, Corollary 2.1 and Appendix A.9; andrews2000boundary; fangSantos2019directional
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Replace the asserted smooth endpoint expansion by a triangular-array continuous-mapping argument for the positive-part square root, followed by conditional analysis under feasibility retention.
seed_details.search_result: Boundary and directional-bootstrap papers do not derive the half-Hölder fourth-root law or the data-dependent truncated kernel generated by leakyIV retention.
seed_details.red_team: Immediate from Andrews because the estimator is merely projected at a boundary.
seed_details.rebuttal: The endpoint is a square root of a regular slack and the implementation conditions on a second random feasibility event, producing a different scale and kernel.

seed_details.title: Matched local-minimax directed-Hausdorff frontier
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Transfer LAN contiguity on the explicit positive-definite covariance path through the square-root set map and impose honest whole-set coverage in the risk comparison.
seed_details.search_result: Hirano--Porter proves nonregularity, while generalized van Trees supplies nonsmooth lower-bound machinery; neither derives the fourth-root leaky-IV set-loss rate or its root-n interior counterpart.
seed_details.red_team: The fourth-root lower bound is a mechanical modulus-of-continuity exercise.
seed_details.rebuttal: Honest random-set coverage, outer directed-Hausdorff loss, fixed relevance, and matching adaptation require a nontrivial two-experiment comparison.

seed_details.title: Uniform numerical or proximal endpoint bootstrap
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Replace derivative estimation by a rescaled local-map approximation for the half-Hölder positive-part square root with unknown local index.
seed_details.search_result: Hong--Li covers nonregular numerical bootstrap and Li covers boundary-uniform constrained estimators, but Li explicitly excludes partial identification and neither treats this endpoint map.
seed_details.red_team: Li's proximal bootstrap already settles arbitrary boundary drift.
seed_details.rebuttal: Its target is a root-n point estimator, whereas the leaky-IV target is a fourth-root set endpoint and whole-set coverage is required.

seed_details.title: Sharp asymptotic excess-loss constant for honest contact hulls
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Solve the Gaussian-shift decision problem induced by whole-set coverage rather than stopping at a positive rate lower bound.
seed_details.search_result: The adjacent nonsmooth-efficiency literature gives general inequalities but no leaky-IV confidence-hull constant.
seed_details.red_team: This is only a constant refinement of S3.
seed_details.rebuttal: An exact minimax constant and attaining critical rule would characterize efficiency in the irregular limit experiment, but the payoff is narrower than the selected adaptive theorem.

seed_details.title: Tangency-order phase diagram across leakage norms
seed_details.anchor: watson2024bounding, Theorem 2 and discussion of general p
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Replace the p=2 quadratic expansion by the local growth order of the distance-to-leakage ball for p=1, p in (1,2), and p greater than 2.
seed_details.search_result: Watson establishes sharp bounds for general p but supplies neither singular-stratum endpoint limits nor rate-adaptive inference.
seed_details.red_team: Changing the norm is a routine p=2-to-general-p extension.
seed_details.rebuttal: Different norm geometries create polyhedral kinks, smooth contacts, and potentially different local rates, although this broader angle is less feasible than the explicit p=2 kernel.

seed_details.title: Many-instrument contact inference
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Debias the minimum-leakage score under regularized covariance estimation before applying multiplier coupling.
seed_details.search_result: The leakyIV documentation recommends shrinkage for large instrument sets but gives no growing-dimension contact theory; searches found no target-method match.
seed_details.red_team: High dimensionality is an ornamental extension.
seed_details.rebuttal: It changes the primitive score rate and therefore the contact endpoint rate, but it adds nuisance-estimation risk before the fixed-dimensional failure is settled.

seed_details.title: Selective feasibility-conditional pivot for retained draws
seed_details.anchor: watson2024bounding, Theorem 4 and Appendix A.9; andrews2000boundary
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Treat bootstrap feasibility as a selection event and condition the Gaussian slack experiment on its realized truncation threshold.
seed_details.search_result: No paper located constructs a selective pivot for leakyIV's retained endpoint samples.
seed_details.red_team: The random truncated kernel already gives the pivot by probability integral transformation.
seed_details.rebuttal: Unknown local drift prevents a directly pivotal transform, leaving a genuine nuisance-index problem, though score inversion offers a cleaner consumer solution.

seed_details.title: Interior semiparametric efficiency bound for leaky-IV endpoints
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Differentiate the covariance endpoint functional and project its influence function onto the nonparametric tangent space.
seed_details.search_result: No named leaky-IV efficiency paper was found, but the fixed-interior endpoint is a smooth finite-dimensional covariance functional.
seed_details.red_team: Immediate from the covariance influence function and ordinary delta method.
seed_details.rebuttal: The objection holds; this lane was dropped rather than presented as novel.

seed_details.title: Ambiguity-robust policy learning with leaky instruments
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Introduce conditional leaky-IV bounds and optimize worst-case welfare over a policy class.
seed_details.search_result: Searches pairing leaky instruments with policy regret found no occupied result, but Watson's maintained homogeneous effect makes policy choice degenerate.
seed_details.red_team: The policy problem is absent from the anchor's model.
seed_details.rebuttal: The objection holds for the specified p=2 homogeneous SEM; pursuing it would require a new model and was dropped.

seed_details.title: Permutation or conformal inversion for contact endpoints
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Identify a symmetry orbit preserving the leaky-IV covariance null and invert its randomization p-values.
seed_details.search_result: Searches found conformal procedures for prediction and synthetic-control counterfactuals, but no assignment or time-permutation symmetry for the observational covariance model.
seed_details.red_team: I.i.d. exchangeability alone does not generate an exact causal-effect null permutation.
seed_details.rebuttal: The objection holds; no valid group action was found, so this lane was dropped.

These establish the coverage architecture but not the adaptive geometric loss result.","multiplier_thread":"Chernozhukov, Chetverikov, and Kato (2013) supply multiplier coupling and anti-concentration for score maxima. The proposed score is a fixed-dimensional quadratic polynomial, but the open step additionally requires uniform integrability and transfer through changing contact geometry.","lower_bound_thread":"Hirano and Porter (2012) prove nonregularity for nondifferentiable functionals. Takatsu and Kuchibhotla (2024) develop generalized van Trees bounds for nonsmooth targets. The exact fixed-relevance Gaussian witness permits a sharper directed-Hausdorff rate comparison.","closest_new_thread":"Li (2025) gives boundary-uniform test inversion for constrained root-n point estimators and explicitly distinguishes that setting from partial identification. Hong and Li (2020) treat numerical bootstrap under drifting sequences. Neither subsumes the proposed whole-set fourth-root kernel."}
